hints: Focus on whether oxidation numbers actually change, which means one species is oxidised while the other is reduced.
Identify each reaction type first: alkene plus bromine, alcohol dehydration, carbonyl addition, and ester hydrolysis.
Check which pair has an element going from 0 to a charged state while carbon also changes, that electron transfer marks the redox pair.
walkthrough:
**Recall what makes a redox reaction**

Remember, redox means electron transfer. One reactant is oxidised (oxidation number increases) and the other is reduced (oxidation number decreases).

Rule to use:
$$\text{redox = change in oxidation number}$$

**Classify each organic reaction**

Let's name what is happening in each pair. This makes it much easier.

$\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CH}_2 + \text{Br}_2$ is electrophilic addition to an alkene. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ with concentrated acid is dehydration to an alkene. $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3 + \text{HCN}$ is nucleophilic addition to a ketone. $\text{HCO}_2\text{C}_2\text{H}_5$ with dilute acid is acid hydrolysis of an ester.

**Test for oxidation number change**

In addition of $\text{Br}_2$ to propene, bromine changes from $0$ in $\text{Br}_2$ to $-1$ in $\text{CH}_3\text{CHBrCH}_2\text{Br}$, so it is reduced. At the same time, the alkene carbons become more positive as they bond to electronegative Br, so they are oxidised.

Simplified equation:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CH}_2 + \text{Br}_2 \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CHBrCH}_2\text{Br}$$

**Confirm the others are not redox**

Dehydration, cyanohydrin formation and ester hydrolysis only rearrange bonds between C, H, O and N with no element gaining or losing electrons overall. Oxidation numbers stay the same, so they are elimination, addition and hydrolysis reactions, not redox.

options.A: Correct. This is electrophilic addition of bromine to the C=C double bond of propene. Bromine is reduced from 0 to -1, while the alkene carbons are oxidised as they form C-Br bonds. Electron transfer occurs, so it is a redox reaction.
options.B: Incorrect. Propan-1-ol with concentrated H3PO4 undergoes acid-catalysed dehydration (elimination) to form propene and water. No oxidation numbers change, the alcohol is not oxidised and phosphorus stays as +5, so this is not redox.
options.C: Incorrect. Propanone with HCN undergoes nucleophilic addition to form a cyanohydrin, CH3C(OH)(CN)CH3. Bonds are formed to C, but carbon and other atoms keep the same oxidation states overall. Students sometimes think addition always means redox, but here there is no electron transfer between oxidant and reductant.
options.D: Incorrect. Ethyl methanoate with dilute H2SO4 undergoes acid hydrolysis to methanoic acid and ethanol. This is a nucleophilic substitution at the carbonyl carbon, breaking the ester into acid plus alcohol with no change in oxidation number, so it is not redox.
